title: Working Near Conveyors
summary: Conveyors can start without warning, catch clothing and drop material on people below. OSHA's conveyor rule sets stops, warnings, guards and lockout for work around them.
talking_points: There must be a way to stop the motor or engine at the operator's station, and an audible warning signal sounded immediately before the conveyor starts up (29 CFR 1926.555(a)(1)).
If the operator's station is remote, there must also be a way to stop the conveyor at the motor or engine location (1926.555(a)(2)).
After an emergency stop, the conveyor cannot restart until the stop switch has been reset to the running or on position (1926.555(a)(3)).
Screw conveyors must be guarded to prevent contact with turning flights (1926.555(a)(4)).
Where a conveyor passes over a work area or walkway, guards must protect the people working or walking below it (1926.555(a)(5)).
All crossovers, aisles and passageways must be conspicuously marked with signs (1926.555(a)(6)).
Lock out or otherwise disable a conveyor and tag it "Do Not Operate" during repairs (1926.555(a)(7)).
Good practice: know where every stop is before you work near a conveyor, and never reach into or step over a running belt.
site_hazards_to_check: No working stop control or start-up warning signal
Emergency stop that restarts the conveyor without being reset
Exposed screw conveyor flights or other unguarded moving parts
Conveyor over a walkway with no guard below
Crossovers and aisles that are not marked
Repairs under way without lockout and a Do Not Operate tag
discussion_questions: Where are the stops on the conveyors we work near, and can we reach them quickly?
Who locks out and tags a conveyor before repairs, and who removes the lock?
Where is it safe to cross the conveyor line on this site?

flags: Verified 1926.555(a)(1)-(7) verbatim; no changes. (a)(8) ANSI B20.1 not used and not cited.
1926.555 is the construction conveyors rule; scope is correct.
